about: What infra-m1.2 took from the legacy capture runners for the one Excel capture adapter (platform/calc-oracle-excel, its worker worker/capture-worker.ps1, and cargo xtask capture) and for CaptureRecord version 2 in tools/calc-verdict. Nothing was ported. Of the 30 runner_candidate inputs infra-m0.4 marked under OxFunc/smart-fuzzer/ and OxFunc/tools/xll-addin/, cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup exits 5 for 18 (numeric provenance unresolved), 3 for 1 (quarantine_derived) and 0 for 11, each of those of disposition reference and outside the release source allowlist. None is a port input without a re-pin, so no re-pin was made, none of the 30 files was opened, and the worker was written fresh from Excel's documented object model (Application, Workbooks.Open, Workbook.SaveAs, Range.Value2, Range.Formula2, Range.HasFormula, Range.SpecialCells, Application.International, CalculateFullRebuild, AutomationSecurity, COMAddIns and COMAddIn.Connect, AddIns2 and AddIn.IsOpen and AddIn.Installed, RegisteredFunctions, Workbook.LinkSources, Workbook.Connections; every add-in state is read, never written, and no Excel option is written beyond the capture's own instance), the COM late-binding call System.__ComObject.InvokeMember (so that a failed property read throws instead of reading as nothing), and the published SpreadsheetML package structure (including the refreshOnLoad of the connections part, of pivot cache definitions and of query tables, the external link part's externalBook, ddeLink and oleLink elements, and the cell metadata index cm that Excel with dynamic arrays writes on a dynamic-array formula). Only this bead writes this file.

legacy_runners_after_this_bead: The legacy runners stay in OxFunc, which this repository never edits; in this repository nothing but calc-oracle-excel drives Excel. Legacy capture data reaches the verdict only through readers: the acquisition labels of migration/evidence/oxfunc-smart-fuzzer.json (cargo xtask evidence labels, infra-m0.6) and calc-verdict's legacy_evidence acquisition (infra-m1.1). No converter of legacy capture bundles into CaptureRecord version 2 exists yet.
verdict_precedent: DnaTreeCalc/src/dnacalc-conform/ is the provenance-first verdict precedent; infra-m1.1 read it for behaviour and recorded that in migration/ports/infra-m1.1.json. This bead extends that one verdict (calc-verdict) and did not read the precedent again.

semantic_changes.change: CaptureRecord version 2: a session (authored revision and operations, calculation-context fingerprint, capture-tool revision, input and output package hashes, capture failures), formula text per inventory cell, each shared-formula range's ref, and the save and reopen round trip (saved caches, reopened raw values). The decoder reads versions 1 and 2; the encoder writes version 2 only.
semantic_changes.reason: Plan section 10.2's capture manifest and the hand-off of infra-m1.1 (2026-10-19).

semantic_changes.change: judge measures a calculated result's revision and context against the run the result set declares and, for a version 2 record, also against the revision and context the capture recorded; a result set at revision R judged against a capture of revision R+1 has every calculated cell stale (revision_not_run). A version 1 record is judged as before.
semantic_changes.reason: infra-m1.1 round-2 judge: stale detection trusted the run identity the result set declared (tools/calc-verdict/src/verdict.rs:529-546 before this bead).

semantic_changes.change: judge refuses a version 2 record whose shared group's listed cells do not cover the group's range ref, whose group cells lie outside it, or whose groups and ranges do not pair one to one.
semantic_changes.reason: infra-m1.1 round-2 judge: version 1 has no shared-formula range, so a record listing C1 and C2 of C1:C3 was judged with a denominator one short.

semantic_changes.change: The infra-m1.1 unit test malformed_records_are_refused_with_their_path now refuses version 3 at capture.version instead of version 2, which is now read.
semantic_changes.reason: Version 2 is a format this bead adds; the refusal of an unknown version is kept.

semantic_changes.change: CaptureRecord version 2 adds an optional "dynamic_array": true on an ordinary formulas entry (FormulaCell::dynamic_array): the workbook saves the formula as a dynamic-array formula over its own cell. It is written only when true, and the decoder refuses it as false or on a shared formula; version 1 records never carry it.
semantic_changes.reason: Review of round 2 (2026-10-19): Excel with dynamic arrays saves a formula such as =MarkUdf() as t="array" with cm="1" over one cell, which the converter refused, so modern packages, untrusted-macro.xlsm and infra-m1.3's fixture among them, would fail capture.

semantic_changes.change: The worker result (dnacalc-capture-worker-result version 1, never committed) carries cm on each formula and may carry the raw value {"unread": "<why>"} for a Value2 read that failed; the converter makes the latter a value failure of the cell.
semantic_changes.reason: Windows PowerShell reads a property whose getter fails as $null without an error, for COM objects too (measured 2026-10-19 in Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100 on an ADODB.Recordset never opened: $rs.RecordCount read as nothing with no error, [double] and [string] of that read gave 0 and an empty string, and InvokeMember of RecordCount threw; transcript and script in target/accept/infra-m1.2/getter-probe.log of the DnaCalc clone, not committed); read plainly, a failed Value2 read would have been recorded as an empty value.

semantic_changes.change: calc-verdict's report (dnacalc-verdict-report) is version 4: a com_add_ins_connected member, after capture_failures, gives the number of COM add-ins the record's environment lists as connected during the capture (the setting com_add_ins_connected, SETTING_COM_ADD_INS_CONNECTED), present when the record carries that setting; and the uncertified reason com_add_in_connected marks a raw comparison against such a record that would otherwise be strict-bit certified (UncertifiedReason::ComAddInConnected, in calc-verdict's seams.json). The two unit tests that asserted version 3 assert 4.
semantic_changes.reason: Round-2 judge (2026-10-21): the committed capture ran with VS15ExcelAdaptor connected, yet its record had no failure and its verdict no count, so the broadening was not counted as honesty rule 2 requires. The orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-21 took counting it in the verdict; bead dc-quhd owns the replacement.

semantic_changes.change: A CaptureRecord setting that lists several things (add_ins, com_add_ins_connected, add_ins_installed, external_links, ole_dde_links, connections) separates items with ; and fields with |, and writes %, ; and | within a field as %25, %3B and %7C. Add-ins are named by ProgId or file name only: add_ins_installed lists names (it listed Name|FullName), and the refusal of an add-in open in the instance names its file name (it named its full path).
semantic_changes.reason: Round-2 judge: the ; and | joins were ambiguous for a name holding either character, and add_ins_installed committed the full local paths of the owner's development add-ins; the orchestrator's privacy ruling of 2026-10-21: add-in names only, never a path, in the record, the verdict and the receipts.

semantic_changes.change: The worker records opened_read_only, the input workbook's Workbook.ReadOnly as Excel opened it, and the excel route of infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook requires it to be true.
semantic_changes.reason: Round-2 judge: the call of Workbooks.Open through InvokeMember, the branch real Excel takes, was evidenced only indirectly; Excel's own ReadOnly shows that the third argument reached Excel.

external_routes.about: The routes from a captured workbook to external data or another application, as the worker handles them (platform/calc-oracle-excel/worker/capture-worker.ps1, its header; src/lib.rs, the module documentation). A route listed under checked is refused before Excel starts, or refuses the capture as an isolation failure; any route not listed under checked is not modeled: the capture neither detects nor refuses it, and nothing in the record says it was absent.
checked_before_excel_starts: a data connection of the connections part with refreshOnLoad (fixture tests/fixtures/worker/external-content.xlsx)
a pivot cache definition with refreshOnLoad, found by the root element of every package part whose first bytes are XML, whatever its name (tests/fixtures/worker/pivot-refresh.xlsx)
a query table with refreshOnLoad, found the same way (tests/fixtures/worker/query-table-refresh.xlsx)
an external link part that is not a link to another workbook: ddeLink, oleLink, or a part of no known kind (tests/fixtures/worker/external-content.xlsx)

a call to RTD, WEBSERVICE (and so FILTERXML over it), IMAGE, STOCKHISTORY, CUBEKPIMEMBER, CUBEMEMBER, CUBEMEMBERPROPERTY, CUBERANKEDMEMBER, CUBESET, CUBESETCOUNT, CUBEVALUE, TRANSLATE, DETECTLANGUAGE, COPILOT, PY, IMPORTTEXT, IMPORTCSV, CALL, REGISTER.ID or SQL.REQUEST (the worker's $ExternalDataFunctions), matched without regard to case on the function name after any _xl prefix and outside string literals, in a cell formula of a worksheet, macro sheet or dialog sheet, in a conditional-formatting or data-validation formula of such a sheet (any element f, formula, formula1 or formula2), or in a defined name (tests/fixtures/worker/external-functions.xlsx)
checked_after_excel_starts: an add-in that is open in the capture's Excel instance (one installed in the profile but not open is recorded only), an add-in of AddIns2 whose state cannot be read, and registered XLL functions: the capture is refused before the workbook is opened, each named by its file name, and no add-in is switched off

a connected COM add-in: not refused and not disconnected (the worker writes no add-in's state). It is recorded by name in the setting com_add_ins_connected (ProgId|Description), every installed add-in of Application.AddIns by its Name, a file name, in add_ins_installed, and no add-in is recorded by a path; each field of these lists writes %, ; and | as %25, %3B and %7C. calc-verdict counts the condition: the report (version 4) carries com_add_ins_connected, the number of COM add-ins the record lists as connected (1 in tools/calc-verdict/tests/captures/infra_m1_2/replay.verdict.json), and a raw comparison against such a record is uncertified with the reason com_add_in_connected where it would otherwise be strict-bit certified (unit test verdict::tests::a_connected_com_add_in_is_counted_and_certifies_no_target). This deviates from the Do, which says 'opening fixtures with macros/add-ins/external links disabled'; the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-21 took counting (option (b) of the round-2 judge). On the owner's machine the COM add-in VS15ExcelAdaptor (registered under HKLM with LoadBehavior 3, read 2026-10-21) read as connected in every automation instance measured. The safe-mode route (Excel started with /safe and attached through AccessibleObjectFromWindow) was tried once in round 1 and was not reliable: startup prompts left by force-stopped instances blocked later starts. Bead dc-quhd (it depends on infra-m1.2) owns capturing in an Excel instance with no COM add-in connected and no setting written, and measures the safe-mode route. A COM add-in whose state or names cannot be read is an environment failure.
links to other workbooks: kept, opened with UpdateLinks 0, which never refreshes them, and recorded in the external_links setting
an OLE or DDE link that Excel reports, and a data connection that Excel reports as refreshing on open or whose setting cannot be read: isolation failures that refuse the capture
not_modeled: an OLE object embedded in a sheet
a linked data type (rich values, such as Stocks or Geography)
a function of an add-in, or a user-defined function, whose name is not in the list above

what a connected COM add-in does during the capture (its handlers of Excel's events, the functions it provides): the verdict counts every capture taken with one and certifies no raw comparison against it; bead dc-quhd owns capturing without one
a formula outside the parts listed above (a chart series, a pivot table calculated field, an XML map, a Power Query mashup without a connection that refreshes on load)
an external-data function added to Excel after the list above was written
any other route not listed under checked

fixtures.generator: platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/fixtures/make-fixtures.ps1 (sha256 c21bdcac29caaee12263d2224bcf71cbae4aaafaa221716e699363bb49e70686) writes each package marked make-fixtures.ps1 below as UTF-8 XML parts, stored (ZIP method 0) with the timestamp 1980-01-01 00:00, by a ZIP writer in the script; run with -OutDir platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/fixtures it rewrites them. The unit test fixtures_are_the_output_of_their_generator (src/worker_tests.rs) runs it into a fresh directory and compares every file with the committed one byte for byte. Round 3 replaced the round 1 and 2 files, which scripts outside the repository had written, with this output: the parts keep their cells, formulas, links, connections and sheets, and differ in namespace declarations, the styles part, override order and relationship IDs. Round 2 of the resumed run (2026-10-21) corrected the generator's content-type overrides (a part's name and its content type were joined into one PartName with an empty ContentType; measured 2026-10-21, Excel 16.0.20430 failed Open of the previous dynamic-array.xlsx, spill.xlsx and untrusted-link.xlsx through the worker's Open-Workbook and opened the regenerated dynamic-array.xlsx and spill.xlsx read-only), which regenerated every package it writes, dc-xb26's three spill fixtures among them.

files.made_by: written by hand in this bead: the stand-in worker of the isolation part of infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook

authored 2026-10-21 in Excel 16.0.20430.20182 through COM automation (Windows PowerShell 5.1; Trust access to the VBA project object model was already enabled for the user, and no setting was changed), by the steps at the top of platform/calc-oracle-excel/tests/acceptance.rs: Workbooks.Add with Sheet1!A1 = 1 and B1 = =A1*2; Workbook_Open added to the workbook's own document module, found by Workbook.CodeName (ThisWorkbook), not by component type; Auto_Open, MarkRan and MarkUdf in a new standard module Module1; Workbook.RemovePersonalInformation set; SaveAs xlOpenXMLWorkbookMacroEnabled with A1 still 1; =MarkUdf() entered in Sheet1!C1 through Formula2, which showed 7 and wrote macro-ran.txt (MarkUdf); Save, with Application.DisplayAlerts off, so no privacy warning was shown or confirmed; the macro-ran.txt deleted. olevba 0.60.2 shows Workbook_Open in VBA/ThisWorkbook, no code in VBA/Sheet1, and Auto_Open, MarkRan and MarkUdf in VBA/Module1. docProps/core.xml has empty dc:creator and cp:lastModifiedBy, docProps/app.xml an empty Company, xl/workbook.xml no x15ac:absPath (workbookPr filterPrivacy=1), and no part holds the user's or the clone's name. Excel saved C1 as a single-cell dynamic-array formula (t=array, ref C1, cm 1). The authoring script and its log are in target/accept/infra-m1.2/round2/ of the DnaCalc-cdoc clone, not committed.
